title: Google researchers find a way to keep self-improving AI agents from memorizing their tests
key_facts: Google Cloud AI Research and several universities describe a method, RRSI (Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses)
A harness is the framework of prompts, tools, memory and logic around a fixed language model
Self-optimizing harnesses tend to memorize their test tasks, so gains on unseen tasks shrink
RRSI caps how many edits a change can bundle, shrinks that cap over time, and uses a critic to reject benchmark-specific hardcoding
Tested on eight benchmarks with Claude Opus 4.8 frozen, per the paper
Up to 14.1 points gain on training tasks and up to 4.7 on five unseen benchmarks, about 30% fewer tokens than the unregularized version
Study covers only harnesses around frozen models
quote_evidence: Because the agent keeps working on the same limited set of test tasks, it ends up memorizing them.
According to the paper, RRSI gains up to 14.1 points on the tasks it was trained on and up to 4.7 points on five benchmarks it never saw.
why_it_matters_hint: Guards against self-improving agents that only look better because they memorized their tests.
notes: Paper results reported by The Decoder; no outside review mentioned.
